subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls and routing policies
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hansen <sam.hansen@fintechco.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls and routing policies

Hi Sam / Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, what success looks like, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points / needs (as discussed)
- Per-customer rate limits and quota enforcement (both steady-state and burst handling).
- Per-customer routing/policy control (ability to route specific tenants to premium model variants or dedicated capacity).
- Tiering and plan-based policies (free / standard / premium) with overrides for high-value tenants.
- Strong tenant isolation for logs, auditing, and data access controls (compliance requirements).
- Predictable cost attribution per tenant and ability to cap spend per org.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Fronting API gateway + home-grown proxy for tenant routing.
- Postgres for tenant config and billing tagging.
- No dedicated LLM serving infra today; currently using a mix of cloud-hosted endpoints and local batching for internal POCs.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- Per-tenant rate limiting with easy admin controls and overrides.
- Configurable routing policies (routing by tenant -> model variant or capacity pool).
- Ability to support 3-tier plans with clear SLAs for premium tenants (target p50/p95 latency goals).
- Reasonable cost predictability and reporting to map spend to tenants.
- Audit logs retention of 12+ months (compliance team requirement).

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a short requirements doc and a proposed POA (multi-tenancy-reqs.pdf, proposed-poa.xlsx).
2) Technical deep-dive: suggest a 60–90m session to go deeper on routing, quotas, and expected traffic patterns (please confirm availability; Sam you mentioned July 13 possibly).
3) We’ll prepare an initial technical approach: default quota suggestions, routing policy examples, and a cost/bandwidth estimate for dedicated capacity.
4) We’ll include a compliance checklist for logs/retention and KMS integration options.

If that all matches, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and loop in Dylan (security/compliance) and Marissa (solutions architect) to prepare the materials.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachment: multi-tenancy-reqs.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
Attachment: proposed-poa.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)
From: Sam Hansen <sam.hansen@fintechco.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls and routing policies

Thanks Alex — that summary looks right. A couple of clarifications / additions:

- Tenant scale: we have ~120 active tenants today; expected growth to ~400 within 12 months.
- Traffic: steady-state avg ~1,200 QPS across customers with periodic bursts up to ~5,000 QPS for market open events.
- Quotas: need both rate-based and token-based quotas (e.g., tokens/min and requests/min) and org-level overrides for enterprise customers.
- Routing: premium tenants should be able to opt into a dedicated model variant or a dedicated capacity pool (we need controls to pin them to a specific variant).
- Compliance: SOC2 and PCI-adjacent posture; logs retention requirement is 12 months, and we need per-tenant access logs for audits.

We’d love a cost ballpark for a dedicated capacity option (monthly) and a rough timeline for getting the routing/quota controls into a PoC.

July 13 for the technical deep-dive works for me; Emily will confirm tomorrow. Please add Dylan and Marissa to the invite.

Thanks —
Sam Hansen
Director of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
sam.hansen@fintechco.com | (212) 555-0147
